overview.title: Overview
overview.byCategoryEmpty: Once you import transactions, you’ll see where your money goes here.
overview.getStartedHint: Two steps to a working budget.
overview.stepBackupBody: Encrypted, daily, to a folder or drive you choose.
overview.stepAccountsBody: Give each account a name, and the bank if you like.
overview.noBudgets: No budgets set for this month
overview.uncategorized_one: {{count}} transaction this month has no category yet.
overview.uncategorized_other: {{count}} transactions this month have no category yet.
overview.trendHint: Income and spending, transfers between your own accounts left out.
overview.reviewPrompt: Review {{month}} for me (use summary_review for {{iso}}). How did income and spending compare with earlier months, which categories changed most, which budgets went over, and which payments stand out? End with one or two practical tips. Keep it short.
overview.firstTip: Tip: give uncategorised transactions a category, and your budgets fill in by themselves.

start.title: Let’s get your money in
start.subtitle: Start with your bank’s transactions. You can change everything later.
start.importBody: A CSV export or PDF statement. Kasboek shows every row before anything is saved.
start.manualBody: Type in your first transaction yourself.
start.needAccount: First add the account it belongs to.
start.restoreTitle: Restore a backup or move computers
start.restoreBody: Open a .kasboek backup or export. This replaces what’s here.
start.privacy: Everything stays on this computer, encrypted.
start.privacyCloud: Your data stays on this computer, encrypted. When you ask the assistant something, your question and the data it needs go to {{aiCompany}}; account numbers are hidden.
start.askAssistant: Not sure where to start? Ask the assistant
start.accountStep: Step 1 of 2 · Which account is this for?
start.doneBody_one: {{count}} transaction from {{account}} is in. Here’s your month.
start.doneBody_other: {{count}} transactions from {{account}} are in. Here’s your month.

transactions.title: Transactions
transactions.subtitle: Every payment in and out, across all accounts.
transactions.emptyBody: Import a CSV export or PDF statement from your bank to get started.
transactions.refundHint: Money back in a spending category (a refund, or someone paying their share) lowers that spending; it doesn’t count as income.

budgets.title: Budgets
budgets.hint: Spending counts money out minus refunds. Transfers between your own accounts don’t count.
budgets.emptyHint: No budgets for this month yet. Type an amount next to a category, or copy last month’s.
budgets.rulesHint: Rules put transactions in a category automatically when the text matches. They apply to imports and, when created, to uncategorised transactions.
budgets.rulesOrder: When several rules match, the one highest in this list wins.
budgets.reach_one: Matches {{count}} transaction, {{uncategorised}} of them without a category.
budgets.reach_other: Matches {{count}} transactions, {{uncategorised}} of them without a category.
budgets.reachOther_one: {{count}} is already in another category and stays there.
budgets.reachOther_other: {{count}} are already in another category and stay there.
budgets.reachWord: Short texts only match as a whole word.
budgets.ibanHint: The counterparty’s account number, exactly. Good for transfers to your own accounts.

import.title: Import
import.subtitle: Bring in CSV exports or PDF statements from your bank. Nothing is saved until you approve.
import.dropTitle: Drop a CSV export or PDF statement here
import.dropBody: Kasboek reads the file, recognises the bank, flags duplicates and problems, and suggests categories. You review everything before it’s saved.
import.needAccount: Add the bank account first, so Kasboek knows where these transactions belong.
import.choose: Choose CSV, PDF or XML file…
import.undoConfirm_one: Remove the {{count}} transaction from this import?
import.undoConfirm_other: Remove the {{count}} transactions from this import?
import.noMapping: Kasboek couldn’t tell which columns hold the date and amount. Choose them under Columns.

issue.balance_mismatch: balance does not follow from the row before
issue.possible_duplicate: looks like a transaction already in Kasboek

import.columnsHint: Tell Kasboek which column holds what. The first row of data is shown in brackets.
import.invert: Flip signs (money out is positive in this file)
import.fixAmount: Enter the amount, negative for money out (e.g. -12,50)
import.checked: {{ai}} checked the file. See the notes above the rows.
import.checkPrivacy: Shows what is sent to {{aiCompany}} and asks before the first check.
import.claudeOff: Set up an assistant in Settings to have it check files.
import.anyBank: Works with CSV exports from any bank: Kasboek reads the column names (Dutch, French, English or German) and remembers each layout after the first import. PDF statements with a table of transactions are read on this computer; nothing is sent anywhere. If a PDF can’t be read that way, you can choose to have the assistant read its text; that is only sent after you agree. XML statements (CAMT.053, offered by many European banks) are read on this computer too: amounts, dates, names and balances come straight from the file.
import.checkPrivacyLocal: Shows what is sent to {{ai}} on this computer or network and asks before the first check.
import.checkSlowHint: Large files are checked in parts, a few at a time. Each part stops by itself after 4 minutes.
import.allKnown: Everything in this file is already in Kasboek ({{from}} – {{to}}).
import.allKnownHint: {{name}} can still sort the transactions of this account that have no category yet.

check.title: What {{name}} did
check.already: {{count}} of {{total}} rows were already in Kasboek and weren’t checked again.
check.renamed_one: Made the name or description readable for {{count}} row
check.renamed_other: Made the name or description readable for {{count}} rows
check.nothingChanged: Nothing in this file needed changing.
check.proposals: Suggestions (only applied when you accept them)
check.rulesTitle: Rules, so future imports are categorised automatically
check.skippedSince_one: {{count}} already had a category by then and was left alone.
check.skippedSince_other: {{count}} already had a category by then and were left alone.
check.saved: Saved: {{rules}} rule(s) and {{count}} categorised transaction(s). Undoing the check doesn’t undo these; change them in Rules or Transactions.

import.transfersPaired_one: {{count}} transfer between your accounts was paired.
import.transfersPaired_other: {{count}} transfers between your accounts were paired.
import.transfersSuggested_one: {{count}} possible transfer to check under Transactions → Transfers.
import.transfersSuggested_other: {{count}} possible transfers to check under Transactions → Transfers.

pdf.balanceOk: The amounts add up to the closing balance on the statement.
pdf.balanceMismatch: The rows don’t add up to the statement: difference {{amount}}.
pdf.runningMismatch_one: {{count}} row doesn’t match the running balance.
pdf.runningMismatch_other: {{count}} rows don’t match the running balance.
pdf.flipHint: If this is a credit card statement, try flipping the signs.
pdf.noTable: Kasboek couldn’t find the transactions table in this PDF.

note.other_account: This statement seems to be for {{iban}}, not this account. Check that you chose the right account.
note.dates_without_year: The statement shows dates without a year; Kasboek used the statement period.
note.pages_without_text_one: {{count}} page had no readable text and was skipped.
note.pages_without_text_other: {{count}} pages had no readable text and were skipped.
note.no_table: No table was found. Pages read: {{pages}}, lines of text: {{lines}}.

ai.hintRemote: Sends the statement’s text, with account and card numbers hidden, to {{aiCompany}} after you agree.
ai.hintLocal: Sends the statement’s text, with account and card numbers hidden, to {{ai}} on this computer or network after you agree.
ai.off: Set up an assistant to have it read this statement.
ai.title: Read this statement with {{ai}}
ai.introNoTable: Kasboek couldn’t read the transactions table in this PDF by itself. {{ai}} can read the statement’s text and point out the transactions.
ai.introMismatch: The rows Kasboek read from this PDF don’t add up to the statement. {{ai}} can read the statement’s text and point out the transactions.
ai.sendsRemote_one: This sends the text of {{count}} page to {{aiCompany}}: dates, amounts, descriptions and the names of who you paid or who paid you.
ai.sendsRemote_other: This sends the text of {{count}} pages to {{aiCompany}}: dates, amounts, descriptions and the names of who you paid or who paid you.
ai.sendsLocal_one: This sends the text of {{count}} page only to {{ai}} on this computer or network: dates, amounts, descriptions and the names of who you paid or who paid you.
ai.sendsLocal_other: This sends the text of {{count}} pages only to {{ai}} on this computer or network: dates, amounts, descriptions and the names of who you paid or who paid you.
ai.hiddenTop: Account and card numbers, e-mail addresses and phone numbers are hidden, only the rows of the transaction table are sent (everything above the table, and the top of every later page, where your name and address usually are, is left out), and the PDF itself is not sent.
ai.verify: Kasboek reads every amount from the PDF’s own text and shows every row before anything is saved.
ai.done: {{ai}} read the statement. Check every row before importing.
ai.replaces: Changes you made to rows so far are replaced by the assistant’s reading.
ai.edited_one: {{count}} row you edited will be replaced.
ai.edited_other: {{count}} rows you edited will be replaced.

pdf.askBank: Ask your bank for a CSV export of this statement, or for a PDF with a table of transactions.

import.lockedWhileAssisting: {{ai}} is working on these rows. Changes made now would be lost, so editing is off until it is done.

consent.title: Check this file with {{ai}}
consent.intro: {{ai}} can check this file: read the columns, point out rows that look wrong, and suggest categories, readable names and rules.
consent.sendsRemote: This sends {{aiCompany}} the names and descriptions of the payments in this file and of your transactions that still have no category, the first rows of the file as they are written, the list of your categories and rules, and any notes the assistant has remembered. Account and card numbers are hidden.
consent.sendsLocal: This sends {{ai}} on this computer or network the names and descriptions of the payments in this file and of your transactions that still have no category, the first rows of the file as they are written, the list of your categories and rules, and any notes the assistant has remembered. Account and card numbers are hidden. Nothing goes to an online service.
consent.notSent: Not sent: the rest of the file, transactions that already have a category, your other accounts.
consent.again: You’re asked again if you switch provider, address or model. Nothing is saved until you have looked at the result.

note.other_account: This statement seems to be for {{iban}}, not this account. Check that you chose the right account.
note.accounts_left_out_one: {{count}} other account in this file was left out.
note.accounts_left_out_other: {{count}} other accounts in this file were left out.
note.not_booked_one: {{count}} entry that is not booked (pending or for information only) was left out.
note.not_booked_other: {{count}} entries that are not booked (pending or for information only) were left out.

import.anyBankLocal: Works with CSV exports from any bank: Kasboek reads the column names (Dutch, French, English or German) and remembers each layout after the first import. PDF statements with a table of transactions are read on this computer; nothing is sent anywhere. XML statements (CAMT.053, offered by many European banks) are read on this computer too: amounts, dates, names and balances come straight from the file.

assistant.title: {{ai}}
assistant.intro: Ask about your money, or let {{ai}} make changes. Anything that changes your data waits for your OK.
assistant.example1: How much did I spend on groceries last month?
assistant.example2: Set my eating-out budget to €150 a month.
assistant.example3: Put my uncategorised transactions in the right categories.
assistant.setupBody: Connect an AI assistant (Claude, Mistral, Gemini, a local model and more) to ask questions about your budget, set budgets, sort transactions and check CSV files.
assistant.privacy: Your messages, and the data {{ai}} looks up to answer them, are sent to {{aiCompany}}. Nothing is sent until you ask something. Account and card numbers are hidden before anything is sent.
assistant.pageContextHint: Tells the assistant which page you have open: the filters, the selected transaction and the rows you see (at most 50), so “this one” works. Account and card numbers are masked. It is sent with your message, like other data the assistant uses.
assistant.privacyLocal: {{ai}} runs on this computer or your network: your messages and data are sent only there.
assistant.checkDone: Checked {{file}}: {{categorised}} categorised, {{renamed}} renamed, {{rules}} rules and {{existing}} older groups suggested. See the import screen.
assistant.reasoningHint: How much the model thinks before answering: less is faster and cheaper, more helps with harder questions. Not every model has this setting; if a model refuses it, Kasboek asks without it.
assistant.reasoningUnsupported: This model doesn't take a reasoning setting and uses its own.
assistant.autoFailed: Tried without asking, but it didn’t work:
assistant.enabledHint: Turn off to hide the assistant and every feature that sends text to an AI provider; Kasboek then works fully on its own.

settings.title: Settings
settings.ibanOptional: Optional. Helps match transfers between your own accounts.
settings.languageHint: Also used for month names. Number and date formats are set separately.
settings.backupsHint: Automatic, encrypted backups in the same format as an export. They open only with Import and your login.
settings.autoHint: Encrypted backups to a folder you choose. A synced folder (OneDrive, iCloud Drive, Dropbox) or a USB drive works well.
settings.securityHint: How your data is protected on this computer.
settings.keyStorageWeak: Not protected: no system keyring found
settings.keyStorageWeakHint: On Linux, install and unlock GNOME Keyring or KWallet, then restart Kasboek.
settings.passwordlessExplain: You’ll unlock Kasboek with {{name}} instead of a password. Your password stops working. A password is stronger: passwordless relies on your computer account.
settings.oldExportsNote: Exports and backups made earlier keep opening with the password that was current then.
settings.twoFactorHint: A 6-digit code from your phone, at every unlock and import.
settings.twoFactorOffBody: Enter a current code to confirm.
settings.recoveryHint: For a forgotten password or lost phone. Making a new one makes the old one stop working on this computer.
settings.newRecoveryBody: The current recovery key will stop working here. Exports made earlier still open with the old one.
settings.autoLockHint: Also locks when the screen locks or the computer sleeps.
settings.keepInTray: Keep Kasboek running in the tray when I close the window
settings.keepInTrayHint: Off: closing the window quits Kasboek. On: Kasboek stays in the tray (the menu bar on a Mac) so Claude can keep using it. Open it again from the tray icon or its shortcut.
settings.hideNumbersHint: Show only the country and the last 4 characters of an account number (BE…1234), in case someone is watching. Hold the eye next to a number to see it for as long as you press. Exports and backups are not changed.
settings.holdToShowNumberOf: Hold to show the account number of {{name}}
settings.insightsHint: Tips found from your own data, on this computer. Nothing is sent unless you press “Get tips” and agreed to it: then the assistant gets a short, masked summary to write them.
settings.encryptionHint: Your budget data is encrypted on disk.
settings.keyStorageOsHint: Data is locked to this computer and user account.
settings.rememberedHint: Remembered on this computer until {{date}}. Other computers, imports and exports still ask for the code.
settings.forgotten: This computer will ask for the code again.
settings.whenBackupHint: Shortly after imports, restores and big changes, at most hourly after other changes, daily regardless, and when Kasboek locks or closes. Kept: everything from the last 24 hours, one per day for 30 days, one per month for a year.
settings.bankNameHint: Optional. Any bank, as you call it.
settings.formatsHint: Each part can be set on its own. Example: {{value}}
settings.accountCurrencyChange: Its {{from}} transactions will count as {{to}}. Use this to correct a wrong currency.
settings.accountKindInvestment: Record its value now and then on the Accounts page; deposits and withdrawals come from its transactions.
settings.fxCostHint: Optional. What this bank charges on top of the exchange rate when it converts money to another currency, e.g. 1.5. Helps Kasboek recognise transfers between your accounts in different currencies.

graphics.label: Graphics card
graphics.hint: Without the graphics card Kasboek may scroll a little less smoothly, and it shows correctly on every computer. A change takes effect after a restart.
graphics.restartHint: Restart Kasboek to use the new choice.
graphics.nowOn: Kasboek now draws with the graphics card.

nowOff.setting: Kasboek now draws without the graphics card, as you chose.
nowOff.windows-arm: Kasboek now draws without the graphics card: on Windows on ARM, graphics drivers can leave the window white.
nowOff.failed: Kasboek now draws without the graphics card: it did not show Kasboek on an earlier start.
nowOff.flag: Kasboek now draws without the graphics card: it was started with --disable-gpu.

settings.insightsHintLocal: Tips found from your own data, on this computer. Nothing is sent anywhere.

auth.welcomeBody: Your budget stays on this computer, encrypted. First, choose how you’ll unlock it.
auth.welcomeLegacy: Your existing data will be kept. Choose how you’ll unlock it from now on.
auth.choosePasswordBody: Strongest option. Works on every computer.
auth.chooseDeviceBody: Passwordless: unlock with your face, fingerprint or PIN.
auth.chooseImportBody: Open an export made with Kasboek, using its login details.
auth.passwordIntro: Use at least 12 characters. Easiest: a few random words with a capital and a number, like kraan-tulp-Ober-7-fiets-mist. Don’t use it anywhere else.
auth.recoveryBody: If you forget your password or lose your phone, this key is the only way back in. It’s shown once.
auth.recoveryTip1: Write it on paper, or store it in a password manager.
auth.recoveryTip2: Don’t keep it in a file on this computer.
auth.recoveryTip3: Kasboek can’t show it again. You can make a new one in Settings.
auth.recoverySaved: I’ve stored my recovery key somewhere safe.
auth.recoveryConfirm: Type the last group of 4 characters to confirm
auth.copied: Copied. Paste it somewhere safe, then clear your clipboard.
auth.copyFailed: Couldn’t copy. Please write it down.
auth.totpBody: Recommended. Besides your password, you’ll enter a 6-digit code from an app on your phone.
auth.totpStep1: Open an authenticator app (Microsoft Authenticator, Google Authenticator, 1Password, …).
auth.totpStep2: Scan this code, or type the key.
auth.totpStep3: Enter the 6-digit code the app shows
auth.totpLater: You can change this later in Settings → Security.
auth.qrAlt: QR code for your authenticator app
auth.recoveryUnlockBody: Enter the recovery key you saved when you set up Kasboek. You’ll choose a new password next.
auth.recoveredBody: You unlocked with your recovery key. Choose a new password to keep Kasboek secure.
auth.eraseBody: Sets all Kasboek data on this computer aside and starts fresh. Everything, including the safety backups, is kept encrypted in quarantine for 30 days. Within that time you can restore it from the Setup screen with the original password or recovery key. After 30 days it is permanently deleted. Exports and backups elsewhere are not touched.
auth.restoredBackup: Kasboek restored its safety copy of the account file from {{date}}. If you changed your password or two-step sign-in since then, change it again.

open.keyMissing: Kasboek’s data is locked with a key that Windows keeps next to it, and the Windows key file (Local State) is missing from Kasboek’s data folder, so the data can’t be unlocked here. This happens when the folder was copied without that file, or from another computer or login. Your password and recovery key can’t help; a backup or export (.kasboek file) can.
open.sealed: Kasboek’s data is locked with a key that your operating system keeps for this login (Windows, macOS Keychain or a Linux keyring), and that key can’t be read on this computer or user account right now. This happens when the data folder was copied from another computer or login, or after the system key was reset. Your password and recovery key can’t help until that key can be read; a backup or export (.kasboek file) can.
open.damaged: Kasboek’s account file is empty or damaged, so the data can’t be opened. This can happen after a power cut or a crash while saving. Kasboek already tried its automatic safety copy of this file. Your password and recovery key can’t help; a backup or export (.kasboek file) can.
open.busy: Kasboek’s account file is busy or can’t be read right now. Antivirus software or a disk problem is a common cause. Try again in a moment: that usually helps.
open.other: Kasboek can’t open its data. Try again, or use a backup or export (.kasboek file).
open.importHint: Choose a .kasboek file. Nothing is erased first: the files that can’t be opened are set aside in the “erased” folder.
open.copied: Copied. It lists file names, sizes and dates only, never your data.
open.eraseExplain: Erase hides all Kasboek data on this computer in an “erased” folder for 30 days, then deletes it for good, and starts fresh. A backup or export is needed to get your data back, so only erase when you have one or no longer need the data.
open.importBody: Choose a .kasboek file and enter its password or recovery key. The files that can’t be opened are kept in the “erased” folder for 30 days, and are only replaced once the imported data opens.

auth.deviceUnavailableHint: Needs Windows Hello or Touch ID, which aren’t available on this computer.
auth.ruleVariety: Three of: lowercase, capitals, numbers, symbols
auth.ruleCommon: Not a common password, and no “Kasboek” in it
auth.rulePattern: No runs like aaaa, 1234 or qwerty
auth.strengthHint: Length matters most. A phrase of random words is strong and easy to remember.
auth.weakBody: Kasboek now asks for stronger passwords to protect your data, especially in backups and exports. Choose a new one to continue.
auth.rememberedNote: Two-factor code remembered on this computer until {{date}}.
auth.deviceChecking: Checking for Windows Hello or Touch ID…
auth.recoveryHidden: The key is hidden now: look it up where you stored it.
auth.restoreErasedBody: Erased data is kept for 30 days and then deleted for good. Choose which copy to restore. It needs the password or recovery key it had.
auth.deviceUnprotectedHint: Needs this computer to protect Kasboek’s key (Windows account, Keychain or a Linux keyring).

transfer.title: Move to another computer
transfer.hint: Copying Kasboek’s data folder doesn’t work: it’s locked to this computer. Use an export instead.
transfer.exportHint: One encrypted file. It only opens with Import in Kasboek and your login: password and 2FA code, or the recovery key.
transfer.importHint: Replace the data here with an export or backup.
transfer.importIntro: Choose a .kasboek file. You’ll need the login details it was made with.
transfer.needsNewPassword: This export used Windows Hello or Touch ID, which isn’t available here. Choose a password for this computer.
transfer.replaceWarning: This replaces everything in Kasboek on this computer. A safety copy of the current data is made first.
transfer.resetNotice: For safety, these were not taken over from the file: {{items}}. Set them up again in Settings.

claude.apiKeyHint: Stored inside your encrypted data. Never shown again.
claude.keyHelp: Create a key in the Anthropic Console and paste it here. Kasboek checks it once with Anthropic.
claude.chatHint: Answers questions and makes changes you approve.
claude.csvHint: Checks and fixes bank exports before import.
claude.privacy: Recommended: Sonnet 5.5 (medium) for chat, Opus 5.5 (medium) for CSV checks. Higher effort is more thorough but slower and costs more. If a request is declined by Anthropic’s safety checks, it’s retried automatically on a fallback model (not available for Haiku).

mcp.title: Claude Desktop & Claude Code (MCP)
mcp.hint: Let Claude apps on this computer read your budget and propose changes while Kasboek is open and unlocked. Account and card numbers are hidden from them.
mcp.note: Works only while Kasboek is running and unlocked. Every change shows up here for you to approve. What Claude reads is sent to Anthropic by that app.
mcp.requestBody: A Claude app connected through MCP wants to make this change:
mcp.desktopUnavailable: Claude Desktop isn’t available on this system.
mcp.codeNotFound: Claude Code wasn’t found on this computer. Use “Set up by hand” below.
mcp.helperMissing: The kasboek-mcp helper is missing from this installation. Reinstall Kasboek.
mcp.addBody: Kasboek will add (or update) only its own entry in this file. Other servers and settings stay as they are.
mcp.removeBody: Kasboek will remove only its own entry from this file.
mcp.backupNote: A copy of the file is saved next to it first. Claude Desktop must be closed completely while Kasboek adds itself (also from the tray icon or menu bar); open it again afterwards.
mcp.addedDesktop: Added. Open Claude Desktop again: Kasboek shows up under Connectors and in the tools menu of a new chat.
mcp.removedDesktop: Removed from Claude Desktop. Restart it to apply.
mcp.codeAdded: Added to Claude Code. Start a new Claude Code session to use it.
mcp.requestExpired: This request waited too long and was declined. Claude can ask again.
mcp.bridgeError: The connection for Claude apps couldn’t start: {{error}}. Kasboek tries again every 30 seconds.
mcp.desktopOpen: Claude Desktop is still open. It saves its own settings when it quits and would remove Kasboek again. Quit it completely first (also from the tray icon or menu bar).
mcp.overwritten: Kasboek was removed from Claude Desktop's settings, probably when Claude Desktop quit. Quit it completely, then add Kasboek again.
mcp.separateNote: Connected Claude apps are separate from the assistant in Kasboek. They have their own switch below and keep working when the assistant is turned off.

fx.title: Currencies
fx.hint: Each account keeps its own currency. Totals, budgets and net worth are shown in the main currency, using the exchange rate of each transaction’s date.
fx.mainHint: Totals and budgets are shown in this currency.
fx.noRate: No exchange rate yet: these amounts are left out of totals. Download the ECB rates or add a rate.
fx.olderThanRates: some transactions are older than the first rate
fx.ecbHint: Downloads the European Central Bank’s public rate list. Nothing about your data is sent.
fx.ecbLast: Last downloaded {{date}}. Only the public rate list is downloaded; nothing about your data is sent.
fx.autoHint: Once a day after unlocking, only when you use other currencies.
fx.manualHint: For a currency the ECB doesn’t publish, or to use your bank’s rate. A rate counts from its date until the next one, and wins over the ECB rate of that day.
fx.dateHint: Used for transactions on and after this date, until the next rate.
fx.unconverted_one: {{count}} transaction this month has no exchange rate.
fx.unconverted_other: {{count}} transactions this month have no exchange rate.
fx.unconvertedHint: They are left out of these totals. Add rates in Settings.

ai.title: Assistant
ai.hint: Choose the AI that answers in Kasboek’s chat and checks CSV files. You use your own account and key with that provider.
ai.providerCloud: Runs at {{company}}, with your own API key and billing.
ai.providerLocal: Runs on this computer or your network. Nothing goes to an online service.
ai.baseUrlLocalHint: Leave empty for the default ({{url}}). Change it if the server runs on another port or computer.
ai.baseUrlCustomHint: The OpenAI-compatible address of the server, ending in /v1 for most servers. Use https unless it runs on this computer or your local network.
ai.keyHint: Your {{name}} API key, stored encrypted in your database.
ai.keyOptional: Only if the server asks for one.
ai.keyHelp: Create a key in your {{name}} account and paste it here. Kasboek checks it once with {{name}}.
ai.chatModelHint: The model name, as the provider writes it.
ai.csvModelHint: Leave empty to use the chat model.
ai.chatDesc: Answers your questions and does what you ask in the chat.
ai.fileDesc: Used when the assistant checks a CSV import or reads a PDF statement. A cheaper model is fine here.
ai.pdfDesc: Used when the assistant reads the text of a PDF statement for you. A cheaper model works well here.
ai.noModelList: This provider does not list its models. Type the model name as the provider writes it.
ai.reloadHint: Press the reload button to fetch the list of models.
ai.note: Pick a model that supports tools (function calling); small local models may answer less reliably. Changes the assistant proposes still wait for your OK.
ai.addProviderHint: Any server that speaks the OpenAI format, such as Ollama Cloud, or one on your own network. Each one keeps its own address, key and models.
ai.providerNameHint: How this provider appears in the list.
ai.keyLocalOptional: Optional for a server on this computer or your local network.
ai.removeConfirm: Its address, models and API key are deleted from this computer. This cannot be undone.

gap.key: Add an API key to finish setting up {{name}}.
gap.url: Enter a valid address to finish setting up {{name}}.
gap.model: Enter a chat model to finish setting up {{name}}.

networth.title: Net worth
networth.subtitle: Everything you own minus what you owe, in your main currency.
networth.unconverted_one: {{count}} account has no exchange rate and is left out. Add rates in Settings → Currencies.
networth.unconverted_other: {{count}} accounts have no exchange rate and are left out. Add rates in Settings → Currencies.
networth.historyHint: At the end of each month, this month up to today.
networth.missingRates_one: {{count}} account without exchange rate left out
networth.missingRates_other: {{count}} accounts without exchange rate left out
networth.empty: Add accounts and transactions to see your net worth grow.
networth.valueHelp: Enter what the account was worth on a day, as your bank or broker shows it. Deposits and withdrawals after that day are added on top until you enter a new value.
networth.noOlder: No older data yet: import older CSV exports to see further back.
networth.startsAt: History starts in {{month}}, with your oldest transaction or recorded value. Import older CSV exports (or record an earlier balance) to see further back.

accounts.title: Accounts
accounts.subtitle: Where your money is, and what you own minus what you owe.
accounts.emptyBody: Start with the account you pay from most, like your current account. Savings, cards and investments can follow later.
accounts.firstHint: Transactions belong to an account. Add that account first.
accounts.archiveHint: Its transactions stay. It is no longer offered for imports or new transactions.
accounts.archiveDiscardAsk: Your changes will not be saved. Archive anyway?

year.title: Year
year.subtitle: Twelve months side by side, and how the years compare.
year.byCategoryHint: Spending is money out minus refunds; transfers between your own accounts are left out.

sync.title: Sync between computers
sync.hint: Keep the same data on several computers through a cloud folder you already use (OneDrive, Google Drive, Dropbox, iCloud Drive). There is no Kasboek server: only encrypted files go into that folder.
sync.startHint: Choose a folder that your cloud app keeps in sync. Kasboek puts a “Kasboek sync” folder inside it.
sync.joinHint: Choose the sync folder another computer already uses. This replaces the data here; you’ll need the password and 2FA code (or the recovery key) of that data.
sync.risk: The encrypted data stays in your cloud folder. If someone gets into that cloud account, your password is what protects it, so keep it long and unique. Passwordless sign-in is set up on each computer separately.
sync.detachedHint: This data syncs through a cloud folder. Choose where that folder is on this computer to keep syncing.
sync.noOthers: No other computer has joined yet.
sync.conflictsHint: Something was changed on two computers at once. The later change was kept; here is what was replaced.
sync.stopHint: The data stays here and on the other computers; they keep syncing with each other.
sync.stopConfirm: This computer stops sending and receiving changes. Its data stays as it is now. To sync again later, join the folder again.

dateInput.invalid: Enter a date as {{format}}, for example {{example}}.

balance.differsSince: Kasboek expected {{expected}}: a difference of {{difference}} since {{date}}.
balance.moreAtBank: Your bank has more: income may be missing, or a payment counted twice.
balance.lessAtBank: Your bank has less: a payment may be missing, or income counted twice.
balance.title: Bank balance · {{name}}
balance.help: Enter the balance your bank shows (in its app or on a statement) at the end of a day. Kasboek counts the account balance from it and compares it with what it expected, so a missing or doubled transaction shows up.
balance.readFromCsv: Balance from the file at the end of {{date}}: {{amount}}.
balance.kasboekOn: Balance in Kasboek at the end of {{date}}: {{amount}}.
balance.ask: What balance does your bank show at the end of {{date}}?
balance.askCompare: Balance at your bank at the end of {{date}}
balance.why: Then Kasboek knows the balance of this account and notices when a transaction is missing. You can also add it later on the Accounts page.
balance.newHint: What your bank shows now. Kasboek counts the balance from here, also when you import older transactions later.

transfers.title: Transfers between your accounts
transfers.hint: Money out of one of your accounts and the same amount into another within 3 days. Paired, both halves count as a transfer: neither income nor spending.

recurring.title: Fixed costs
recurring.subtitle: Subscriptions, rent, insurance and income that come back, found from your transactions.
recurring.emptyBody: After a few months of transactions, Kasboek finds your subscriptions and other fixed costs here.
recurring.hint: Something wrong? Use the menu on a row, then Not a fixed cost.
recurring.noLongerCost: {{name}} is no longer counted as a fixed cost.
recurring.noLongerIncome: {{name}} is no longer counted as fixed income.
recurring.hiddenHint: Payments you said aren’t fixed. They’re left out of the totals above and of balance warnings.
recurring.categoryRule: Also for future payments (adds a rule)
recurring.categoryPartial: The payments were moved, but the rule could not be saved.
recurring.ruleReach_one: The rule matches {{count}} payment in all.
recurring.ruleReach_other: The rule matches {{count}} payments in all.
recurring.ruleReachMore_one: {{count}} of them is not in this list.
recurring.ruleReachMore_other: {{count}} of them are not in this list.
recurring.categoryDone_one: {{count}} payment moved to the new category.
recurring.categoryDone_other: {{count}} payments moved to the new category.

alerts.balance: {{name}} may go below zero before {{date}}: {{lowest}} after {{due}} of fixed costs still due.

goals.title: Savings goals
goals.subtitle: Save towards something, and see what to put aside each month.
goals.emptyBody: A holiday, a car, a buffer: set an amount and a date, and Kasboek shows what to put aside each month.
goals.overdue: The date ({{date}}) has passed; {{left}} to go.
goals.perMonth: Put aside {{amount}} a month to reach it by {{date}}.
goals.name: What for
goals.byHand: I keep it up to date myself

export.csvHint: Save these transactions as a CSV file (for a spreadsheet or your accountant)
export.reportSub: Income and spending per month and per category, transfers between own accounts left out.

permissions.title: What the assistant may do by itself
permissions.hint: Changes the assistant makes wait for your OK, unless you allow that kind of change here. Changes made without asking show in the chat.

modeHint.ask: Every change waits for your OK.
modeHint.smart: Sorting, names, splits, transfers, rules, categories, budgets and goals happen by themselves. Balances, deleting rules, new accounts, importing and the assistant’s memory ask first. Changes to more than {{limit}} transactions always ask.
modeHint.trust: Every change happens by itself, also large ones. A few things still always ask, see the note below.
modeHint.custom: Choose per kind below. Changes to more than {{limit}} transactions always ask.

permissions.trustNote: Still asks first: saving an import read from a PDF, and changes asked for through Claude Desktop or Claude Code (unless you switch that off below). The assistant can never change settings, keys, addresses or its own permissions.

kind.organise: Categories, budgets, goals and fixed costs

kindHint.categorise: Setting categories, readable names and notes, splitting payments, pairing transfers.
kindHint.rules: A rule also sorts existing uncategorised transactions.
kindHint.organise: Adding a category, setting a budget, creating a savings goal, marking a fixed cost as not fixed.
kindHint.balances: Recording a bank balance, an investment value or an exchange rate.
kindHint.import: Saving the ready rows of the open import.
kindHint.memory: Saving or forgetting something in the assistant’s memory. What it remembers is sent along with every chat.

permissions.mcp: Claude Desktop and Claude Code always ask
permissions.mcpHint: Changes asked for by Claude apps over MCP wait for your OK in Kasboek, whatever the mode above. Switch this off to let the mode decide for them too.

memory.title: What the assistant remembers
memory.hint: Facts and preferences for later conversations, such as when you get paid or which category a shop belongs in. Kept encrypted on this computer only: not synced and not given to Claude apps over MCP. They are sent to {{name}} with each message so it can use them.
memory.enabledHint: When off, nothing is remembered and nothing from the memory is sent. What is saved stays until you remove it.
memory.empty: Nothing yet. Ask the assistant to remember something, or add it here.
memory.placeholder: E.g. “I get paid on the 25th” or “Colruyt is Groceries”
memory.full: The memory is full: remove something first.
memory.noNumbers: No account or card numbers, passwords or other secrets: Kasboek refuses numbers that look like an account or card.
memory.forgetAllText: All remembered items ({{count}}) are removed. This can’t be undone.
memory.refused: Kasboek doesn’t remember account or card numbers. Leave the number out.

update.title: Kasboek {{version}} is available
update.readyRestart: Downloaded and checked. Kasboek closes, shows the installation progress in its own window and opens again. This usually takes a minute or two, longer on a slow computer.

ready.dmg: Downloaded and checked. Kasboek opens the disk image; drag Kasboek to Applications and replace the old one.
ready.deb: Downloaded and checked. Kasboek opens the package in your software installer.

update.preparing: Preparing the update… Making a safety copy of your data first.
update.installing: Installing… Kasboek closes, shows the progress and opens again in a moment.

helper.failed: The update could not be installed. Kasboek is starting again.
helper.cancelled: The update was cancelled. Kasboek is starting again.
helper.notClosed: Kasboek did not close in time, so the update was not installed. Kasboek is opening again.
helper.stillWorking: Windows Installer is still working (this can take several minutes).
helper.noProgress: Nothing new for a minute. If a Claude app is open, closing it may help.
helper.slow: Taking long? Download it from the release page:

opened.dmg: Drag Kasboek to Applications and choose Replace. Then quit Kasboek and open it again.
opened.deb: Finish the installation in the software installer, then quit Kasboek and open it again.

update.noFile: This release has no file for this computer. Download it from the release page.
update.safety: Kasboek makes a backup of your data first, and checks the file against the checksum GitHub publishes for it.
update.autoHint: At start and once a day, Kasboek asks GitHub whether there is a newer version. Nothing about your data is sent.
update.devOnly: Updates are only checked in installed versions.
update.availableHint: Version {{version}} is available: use the button at the top.
update.bridgesNote: Claude apps that are connected to Kasboek are disconnected during the update. If one does not reconnect afterwards, restart it.

welcome.aiBody: The assistant answers questions about your money and can make changes for you, which wait for your OK. Choose an AI provider, or skip this and set it up later in Settings.
welcome.local: {{name}} runs on your own computer and needs no key. Start it before you use the assistant.
welcome.privacy: When you use the assistant, your messages and the data it looks up go to {{company}}. Nothing is sent until you ask something. Account and card numbers are hidden before anything is sent.
welcome.updatesBody: Kasboek can tell you when a new version is out. You decide when to install it.
welcome.updatesHint: At start and once a day.
welcome.updatesPrivacy: Kasboek asks GitHub, where Kasboek is published, for the latest version. GitHub sees your IP address; nothing about your data is sent. You can change this in Settings.
welcome.introBody: A budget app that keeps your money matters on your own computer. A few choices and you're ready.
welcome.introPrivateHint: Your data is encrypted and stays on this computer. No account, no Kasboek server.
welcome.introImportHint: Drop a CSV export or PDF statement from your bank; Kasboek shows every row before it saves anything.
welcome.introPlanHint: Budgets, fixed costs, savings goals, a year view and your net worth.
welcome.introAssistant: An assistant, if you want one
welcome.introAssistantHint: Ask questions or let it sort transactions; changes wait for your OK.
welcome.basicsBody: You can change all of this later in Settings.
welcome.safetyBody: Kasboek's data lives only on this computer, so a backup elsewhere matters.
welcome.safetyRecovery: Keep your recovery key somewhere safe: without your password or that key, nobody can open your data, not even Kasboek.
welcome.claudeBody: Already use a Claude app? It can read your budget and propose changes while Kasboek is open and unlocked. Its changes wait for your OK in Kasboek. Optional.
welcome.claudeNote: Kasboek adds only its own entry to the Claude app's settings, and keeps a copy of the file first. Close Claude Desktop completely before adding it, and open it again afterwards.
welcome.codeNotFound: Claude Code wasn’t found on this computer. You can set it up later in Settings.
welcome.formatHint: How amounts, dates and times look. Every part can be set separately in Settings.
welcome.ecbHint: For accounts or payments in other currencies: the European Central Bank's daily reference rates, downloaded now and kept up to date. Only the rates are fetched; nothing about you is sent.
welcome.syncHint: Optional. Keep the same data on your other computers through a cloud folder you already use; only encrypted files go there. You can also do this later in Settings.

tour.label: Tour of Kasboek
tour.settingsHint: A short walk past each part of the app.

step.overview: This month at a glance: income, spending, what's left in your budgets, warnings and your first steps.
step.transactions: Every payment. Search, filter, set categories, rename, split a payment or pair transfers between your own accounts.
step.budgets: Set an amount per category per month and see how much is left. Rules that sort transactions automatically are here too.
step.recurring: Subscriptions, rent, insurance and salary, found from your transactions, with what is still due this month.
step.goals: Save for something: an amount by a date, with what to put aside each month.
step.year: The whole year by month and category, with CSV and PDF export for your taxes or accountant.
step.import: Bring in a CSV export or PDF statement from your bank. Check it with the assistant before you save it.
step.assistant: Open or close the assistant. Ask about your money, or let it make changes that wait for your OK.
step.settings: Backups, sync between computers, the assistant, formats and more.
step.lock: Lock Kasboek when you step away. It also locks by itself after a while.
step.importLocal: Bring in a CSV export or PDF statement from your bank. Nothing is saved until you approve.
step.settingsLocal: Backups, sync between computers, formats and more.
step.accounts: Your accounts and their balances, and your net worth over time. Add an account or check a balance here.
step.importBar: Import is also up here, on every page, so a new statement is always one click away.

webdav.intro: Sync through your own WebDAV server: Nextcloud, ownCloud, Synology, QNAP, Koofr, pCloud or another. Kasboek puts a “Kasboek sync” folder there; only encrypted files go into it. A phone can sync this way too.
webdav.urlHint: For Nextcloud: Files → Settings (bottom left) → WebDAV. Must start with https://, or http:// for a server in your home network.
webdav.passwordHint: Preferably an app password made for Kasboek. It is kept in your encrypted data on this computer only.
webdav.startHint: Instead of a cloud folder: your own server or NAS.

errors.auth_device_unprotected: Windows Hello or Touch ID can only replace the password when this computer protects Kasboek’s key (Windows account, macOS Keychain or a Linux keyring). Choose a password instead.
errors.auth_nothing_erased: There is no erased data to restore.
errors.auth_restore_blocked: Kasboek is already set up here. Erased data can only be restored on the first screen.
errors.auth_erase_failed: Kasboek could not set the data aside, so erasing was stopped. Nothing was deleted.
errors.auth_device_unavailable: Windows Hello could not be started. Try again, or restart Kasboek.
errors.auth_device_not_present: Windows Hello is not set up on this computer: there is no camera, fingerprint reader or PIN available.
errors.auth_device_not_configured: Windows Hello is not set up for your Windows account. Set it up in Windows settings first.
errors.auth_device_disabled: Windows Hello is turned off by a policy on this computer.
errors.auth_device_busy: Windows Hello is busy. Try again in a moment.
errors.auth_device_retries_exhausted: Windows Hello stopped after too many failed attempts. Try again later.
errors.import_not_pdf: This file is not a PDF.
errors.import_is_pdf: This is a PDF file. Open it as a bank statement instead.
errors.import_pdf_password: This PDF is password protected. Remove the password in your PDF viewer or bank app and try again.
errors.import_pdf_broken: This PDF could not be read. The file may be damaged. Download it again from your bank.
errors.import_pdf_too_large: This PDF is too large or too complex to read. Try a PDF of a single statement.
errors.import_pdf_scanned: This PDF has no selectable text (probably a scan or photo). Ask your bank for a CSV, or for a PDF with text.
errors.import_pdf_busy: Another PDF is still being read. Wait a moment and try again.
errors.insights_consent_needed: Agree to send the summary to {{ai}} first.
errors.insights_unchecked: {{ai}}’s tips couldn’t be checked. Try again or choose another model.
errors.insights_too_long: {{ai}}’s answer was too long to fit. Try again, or choose a model with a bigger output limit in Settings → Assistant.
errors.assistant_no_key: Add your API key in Settings → Assistant first.
errors.assistant_no_model: Choose a model in Settings → Assistant first.
errors.assistant_too_long: Part of this was too large for the assistant to answer, even in smaller pieces. Try again, pick a model with a bigger output limit in Settings → Assistant, or split the file.
errors.assistant_timeout: {{ai}} took too long and was stopped. Try again, or pick a faster model for CSV checks in Settings → Assistant.
errors.assistant_bad_plan: {{ai}}’s answer couldn’t be read. Try again, or try another model.
errors.assistant_pdf_not_pdf: This import is not a PDF statement.
errors.assistant_pdf_empty: This PDF has no text to read.
errors.assistant_pdf_no_table: No transaction rows were found in this PDF, so nothing was sent.
errors.assistant_pdf_too_long: This statement has too many pages for the assistant to read (the limit is 40 pages). Try a statement for a shorter period.
errors.assistant_pdf_no_rows: {{ai}} didn’t find transactions that could be matched to the text of this statement. Nothing was changed.
errors.assistant_failed_network: Can’t reach {{ai}}{{detail}}. Check the address and your connection, and that the service is running.
errors.assistant_failed_auth: {{ai}} did not accept the API key{{detail}}. Check it in Settings → Assistant. The key may also not have access to this model.
errors.assistant_failed_rate_limit: {{ai}} is rate-limiting this key right now{{detail}}. Try again in a minute.
errors.assistant_failed_model_not_found: {{ai}} doesn’t know this model or address{{detail}}. Check them in Settings → Assistant.
errors.assistant_failed_bad_request: {{ai}} rejected the request{{detail}}. This model may not support what is needed; try another model.
errors.assistant_failed_unknown: Something went wrong talking to {{ai}}{{detail}}. Try again.
errors.import_xml_not_camt: This XML file is not a bank statement (CAMT.053). Ask your bank for the statement as CAMT.053.
errors.import_xml_broken: This XML file could not be read. The file may be damaged. Download it again from your bank.
errors.import_xml_dtd: This XML file contains a DTD or entity definitions, which Kasboek does not read. A bank statement does not need them.
errors.import_xml_too_large: This XML file is larger than 20 MB or has too many rows. Try a shorter period.
errors.import_xml_version: This version of the CAMT format is not supported. Ask your bank for CAMT.053 in version 001.02 or later.
errors.import_xml_accounts: This file holds statements for more than one account, and none of them is the chosen account. Add the account’s IBAN on the Accounts page, choose that account and open the file again.
errors.import_xml_iban_mismatch: The IBAN in this file is not the IBAN of the chosen account. Choose the account this file belongs to, or correct the IBAN on the Accounts page.
errors.import_xml_currency: This file is in another currency than the chosen account. Choose the account in that currency.
errors.assistant_disabled: The assistant is turned off. Turn it on in Settings → Assistant.

insights.title: Suggestions
insights.staleData: Your data changed since then. Refresh.
insights.askPrompt: Here is a tip from my Overview: “{{tip}}” Can you explain it and help me decide what to do?
insights.setup: Set up an assistant to have these written as personal tips.

consent.title: Get tips from {{ai}}
consent.sendsRemote_one: To write tips, Kasboek sends {{ai}} ({{aiCompany}}) a short summary it made on this computer: {{count}} item such as fixed costs that went up, budgets that went over and payments that stand out, with the payee or category name and rounded amounts. No account or card numbers, no account names, no balances or income, and no list of your transactions. {{ai}} only chooses and words the tips; every amount you see is filled in by Kasboek from your own data. Nothing is changed.
consent.sendsRemote_other: To write tips, Kasboek sends {{ai}} ({{aiCompany}}) a short summary it made on this computer: {{count}} items such as fixed costs that went up, budgets that went over and payments that stand out, with the payee or category name and rounded amounts. No account or card numbers, no account names, no balances or income, and no list of your transactions. {{ai}} only chooses and words the tips; every amount you see is filled in by Kasboek from your own data. Nothing is changed.
consent.sendsLocal_one: To write tips, Kasboek sends {{ai}} on this computer or network a short summary it made on this computer: {{count}} item such as fixed costs that went up, budgets that went over and payments that stand out, with the payee or category name and rounded amounts. No account or card numbers, no account names, no balances or income, and no list of your transactions. Nothing goes to an online service. {{ai}} only chooses and words the tips; every amount you see is filled in by Kasboek from your own data. Nothing is changed.
consent.sendsLocal_other: To write tips, Kasboek sends {{ai}} on this computer or network a short summary it made on this computer: {{count}} items such as fixed costs that went up, budgets that went over and payments that stand out, with the payee or category name and rounded amounts. No account or card numbers, no account names, no balances or income, and no list of your transactions. Nothing goes to an online service. {{ai}} only chooses and words the tips; every amount you see is filled in by Kasboek from your own data. Nothing is changed.
consent.again: You’re asked again if you switch provider, change its address or model. Tips are only made when you press the button.

subscriptions.body: Worth checking now and then whether you still use them all.
